Last year, grown adults were sleeping outside malls for a six-inch monster with teeth.
Resale prices hit hundreds of dollars.
Everyone wanted one, and almost nobody could get one.
It made about ten times more of them.
Scalpers got wiped out, and some Labubus now sell for less than retail.
That should've been the win. Everyone finally gets the toy they wanted.
Instead, sales fell by about half in a single quarter.
In the Americas, by up to seventy-five percent.
And for the first time ever, the Monsters line shrank in the first half of the year.
Labubu isn't dead. It still outsells most of Pop Mart's other characters.
But once everyone could have one... turns out nobody wants one.
